title: Historic Centre of Bukhara
summary: Bukhara, on the Silk Roads and more than 2,000 years old, is described by UNESCO as the most complete example of a medieval Central Asian city, with its urban fabric largely intact. It holds the 10th-century tomb of Ismail Samani and many 17th-century madrasas. It became capital of the Samanid kingdom in 892, was sacked by the Mongols in 1220, and was inscribed as World Heritage in 1993.

uncertainty.note: Start is the year Emir Ismail ibn Ahmad chose Bukhara as capital of the Samanid kingdom (ICOMOS); end is the 1993 UNESCO inscription. The city itself is described as more than 2,000 years old.

as_recorded.value: In 892 Emir Ismail ibn Amad (892-907) created an independent state and chose Bukhara as the capital of the powerful Samanid kingdom (OCR text of ICOMOS PDF, names garbled in the source)
